f.title: Apply the Act to digital personal data processed in India and to processing abroad linked to offering goods or services in India
f.statement: The Act applies to the processing of digital personal data within India where the data are collected in digital form, or in non-digital form and digitised later; and also to processing outside India if it is in connection with any activity related to offering goods or services to Data Principals within India. It does not apply to personal data processed by an individual for personal or domestic purposes, or to personal data made publicly available by the Data Principal or by another person under a legal obligation.
f.clause: Chapter I, section 3 (Application of Act)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023), Gazette of 11 August 2023. Binds Data Fiduciaries, e.g. MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers that determine the purpose and means of processing digital personal data of patients and reporters in adverse-event reports. The Act has no separate category for health data. Provisions come into force on dates the Central Government notifies (s. 1(2)); no date is stated in this text.
f.exceptions: Not applicable to personal data processed for personal or domestic purposes, or made publicly available by the Data Principal or under a legal obligation (s. 3(c)).
f.processes: Regulatory intelligence; Data integrity & records

f.title: Sanctions: penalties up to INR 250 crore for failed security safeguards and INR 200 crore for failed breach notification
f.statement: Where the Board determines after an inquiry that a breach of the Act or the rules is significant, it may impose the monetary penalty in the Schedule: up to INR 250 crore for breach of the obligation to take reasonable security safeguards (s. 8(5)); up to INR 200 crore for failing to notify the Board or affected Data Principals of a personal data breach (s. 8(6)); up to INR 200 crore for children's obligations (s. 9); up to INR 150 crore for Significant Data Fiduciary obligations (s. 10); up to INR 50 crore for any other breach.
f.clause: Chapter VIII, section 33 and the Schedule
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023), Gazette of 11 August 2023. Binds Data Fiduciaries, e.g. MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers that determine the purpose and means of processing digital personal data of patients and reporters in adverse-event reports. The Act has no separate category for health data. Provisions come into force on dates the Central Government notifies (s. 1(2)); no date is stated in this text.
f.processes: Safety governance; Quality system & CAPA
